about: After Communion and the ablutions, Psalm 150 is sung for Lauds of Easter Sunday. A triple Alleluia precedes the psalm and is repeated after its doxology.

seg.tr: Praise the Lord in His sanctuary; praise Him in His majestic firmament.
Praise Him for His great works; praise Him for His supreme majesty.
Praise Him with the blast of a trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and cithara.

ex.w033: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument.
ex.w035: Cithara names an ancient stringed instrument. It is distinct from the psaltery named beside it.

seg.tr: Praise Him with drum and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe.

ex.w040: Here dance accompanies the praise of God.
ex.w045: Here the instrument is understood as a pipe. The word has a broader musical range and does not specify a modern church organ.

seg.tr: Praise Him with resounding cymbals; praise Him with clashing cymbals. Let everything that breathes praise the Lord!

ex.w048: These cymbals are struck plates, not a stringed instrument.

seg.tr: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit,
as it was in the beginning, so it is now and always, forever and ever. Amen.
